Brahmajālasutta
Bud. Pāli. 1st Sutta of Dīghanikāya; on śīla an. speculations about soul. The Chinese Dīghāgama an. text in Tibetan Kanjur correspond to this text.
For a brief summary of the contents see His.. of Pali Lit. I. p.. 81-84.
For a. equation of the 62 views of this Sutta with Upaniṣadic thought see Nalinaksha Dutta, IHQ. VIII-4. 1932, p.. 706-46.
Br. Mus. Pāli p. 137 (2 mss.). Cambr. Uni. Pāli p. 146 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 131-45. 147-49. 151. 1714 (fr.). 1715. 1716. Filliozat II. p. 14. Stockholm Pāli p. 150 (2 mss.).
For the Tibetan text see F. Weller, Uber das Brahmajālasūtra. Asia Major IX (1933) 195-332. [Page157-b]
For a German transl. of Chinese Dīghāgama text by F. Weller see Woolner Commemoration Vol. p.. 260-96.
For a comment on the German transl. see Bruns Schindler, Asia Major, VII. 4 (1932) 642-4.
Pt.. Nalanda Dig. Pāli Ser. Dīghanikāya Vol. I. p.. 1-40. For other Pt.. references see NCC. IX. p.. 56b-57a.
--C. Aṭṭhakathā. Br. Mus. Pāli p. 138.

Brahmajālasūtra
Bud. Skt. a fundamental text of the Tendai sect of Buddhism in Japan. on the origin an. end of the world.
AMG. II. p. 286. AR. XX. p. 483. Nanjio 554. 1087.
C.. Comp. Cat. of Tib. Bud. Canons no. 352.
Q. Abhidharmakośavyākhyā. See La Vallee Poussin, ‘Pāli an. Sanskrit’. JRAS (1903) 359--62; Levi, BMFJ. I. i. 25. 33. 48.
Q. by Nāgārjuna in Prajñāpāramitāśāstra; title restored in Nanjio 1087. see IHQ. III. p. 413.
Transl. into Chinese by Kumārajīva of the Latter Tashin dynasty in 406 A. D.
See Wint. HIL. II. p.. 235. 622.
Ed.. with French transl. by J. J. M. D.. Groot. Le Code du Mahāyāna en Chin.. Verhandelingen der Kon. [Page158-a. Akadamie van Wetenshappen te Amsterdam Amsterdam, 1893.
